     1	"""Single-bulk-amplitude WKB gravity wave drag (Hines-1997-inspired).
     2	
     3	.. warning::
     4	
     5	   This is **NOT** the full Hines (1997) Doppler-spread *spectrum*.  It is
     6	   a single-bulk-amplitude WKB approximation: one rms wave amplitude is
     7	   propagated and saturated per column (see the disclosed-simplification
     8	   note below), rather than the full azimuthal + vertical-wavenumber
     9	   Doppler-spread spectrum.
    10	
    11	Non-orographic GWD scheme: a single bulk wave amplitude grows with
    12	decreasing density and is capped by a smooth saturation amplitude. Uses
    13	bottom-up propagation with smooth sigmoid activation for AD-safety —
    14	differentiable ALMOST EVERYWHERE (the ``clip``/``minimum`` drag-floor and
    15	tendency limiters are subgradient KINKS, not everywhere-smooth).
    16	
    17	.. note::
    18	
    19	   **Disclosed simplification / limitation (F-GWD-2, defer).** This is a
    20	   *single bulk-amplitude* approximation of the Hines spectrum: one rms
    21	   wave amplitude ``sigma`` is propagated and saturated per column rather
    22	   than the full azimuthal + vertical-wavenumber spectrum.  Consequently
    23	   the whole packet saturates at once and the per-level deposition
    24	   ``(sigma_grown^2 - sigma_new^2)·rho`` is large; the ``Fmax`` clip then
    25	   *binds* over a substantial fraction of a realistic column (≈22-40 % of
    26	   levels on 30-60 level grids at the default ``total_rms_wind``), so the
    27	   cap — not the Doppler-spread physics — shapes the drag profile there.
    28	   The drag remains a physically-signed momentum sink and is AD-safe
    29	   (differentiable a.e.; the ``clip``/``minimum`` limiters are subgradient
    30	   kinks, not everywhere-smooth); only its *vertical distribution* is
    31	   cap-dominated.  A
    32	   faithful upgrade (spectral/azimuthal Hines) plus a QBO / momentum-flux
    33	   benchmark is required before retuning ``Fmax`` / ``total_rms_wind`` —
    34	   retuning without a benchmark would be guessing.  Default GWD scheme is
    35	   ``none``; this scheme is opt-in.
    36	
    37	Faithfulness to Hines (1997)
    38	----------------------------
    39	This is a Hines-INSPIRED bulk heuristic, NOT a faithful Hines Doppler-spread parameterization.
    40	The Hines (1997) MECHANISM — an incident azimuthal + vertical-wavenumber SPECTRUM whose
    41	Doppler-shifted cutoff vertical wavenumber evolves with the background wind and the wave-induced
    42	rms wind (eq. 9 is that cutoff-wavenumber relation, NOT a velocity-amplitude cap) — is ABSENT.
    43	This scheme propagates ONE bulk rms amplitude and saturates it against a scalar (per-column, but
    44	locally ``N(z)``-dependent) scale ``σ_sat = N(z)/m_*`` — one amplitude, one scale per level.
    45	FAITHFUL to Hines — only the undamped-WKB amplitude scaling:
    46	  * the amplitude grows with ``1/√ρ`` between levels, ``σ_grown = σ·√(ρ[k+1]/ρ[k])`` — the WKB
    47	    scaling for a conserved ``ρσ²`` (NOTE: ``ρσ²`` is the code's ASSUMED invariant, NOT the true
    48	    momentum flux ``ρ⟨u'w'⟩``, which carries the wave-geometry ``k/m`` correlation omitted here).
    49	DEPARTURES from Hines — the mechanism is gone:
    50	  * **NO Doppler-spread SPECTRUM**: a SINGLE bulk rms amplitude, not the azimuthal +
    51	    vertical-wavenumber spectrum whose cutoff evolution IS the Hines mechanism (F-GWD-2);
    52	  * **NO background-wind coupling in propagation**: the wind is NOT used for Doppler shifting,
    53	    cutoff evolution, critical-level filtering, or refraction — it enters ONLY as (a) the
    54	    antiparallel sink DIRECTION and (b) the tendency limiter (``lat`` and ``p_half`` are unused;
    55	    a resting column can still saturate the packet internally, the projection just zeroes the
    56	    RETURNED vector tendency and heating);
    57	  * ``σ_sat = N/m_*`` is a **bulk saturation-amplitude HEURISTIC** (a velocity scale ≈ the
    58	    intrinsic phase speed ``N/m_*``), NOT Hines eq. 9's cutoff wavenumber;
    59	  * the deposition ``drag = ρ(σ²_grown − σ²_new)`` (where ``σ_new`` is the smoothly-saturated
    60	    amplitude ``σ_grown(1−f)+σ_sat·f``, equal to ``σ_sat`` only in the hard-saturation limit
    61	    ``f→1``) is a per-layer STRESS DECREMENT [Pa] (``accel = −decrement/(ρ·dz)``). Under the
    62	    code's ASSUMED fixed wave geometry/proportionality ``F ∝ ρσ²`` this reads as a stress-flux
    63	    divergence, but it is NOT Hines' spectral vector momentum flux — the azimuthal-spectrum vector
    64	    covariance ``ρ⟨u'w'⟩`` (with its ``k/m`` sign/geometry) that Hines deposits is absent here;
    65	  * the **antiparallel "pure deceleration along U" and the KE→heat closure** (all mean-flow KE
    66	    loss returned as local frictional heating) are bulk-closure DESIGN choices — Hines deposits
    67	    the vector momentum/energy of the dissipating spectrum, which need not be antiparallel to the
    68	    local ``U`` and distinguishes wave-energy dissipation from mean-flow KE dissipation and
    69	    heat-flux (Becker & McLandress 2009);
    70	  * the ``Fmax`` cap and the tendency limiter are **UNCLOSED sinks**: the scan removes the FULL
    71	    uncapped amplitude loss from the wave carry but deposits only the CAPPED stress on the mean
    72	    flow, so excess wave momentum/energy is lost rather than transferred — so even in the
    73	    interior the mean-flow drag no longer equals the wave stress-flux divergence (momentum is
    74	    not conserved; energy of the mean flow that IS removed is still heated back exactly).
    75	NUMERICS (AD-safety): the smooth sigmoid saturation (``doppler_sharpness``) — NOTE this smooth
    76	blend is a two-sided relaxation toward ``σ_sat``, so BELOW threshold (``σ_grown < σ_sat``, where
    77	``f_diss`` is small but nonzero) it nudges the carry amplitude slightly UP toward ``σ_sat`` (a weak
    78	spurious SOURCE); the drag clamp ``[0, Fmax]`` floors the resulting negative decrement to 0, so this
    79	sub-threshold gain is neither drag nor heat but an unbudgeted carry perturbation of the AD smoothing
    80	(a hard ``σ_grown > σ_sat`` gate would not have it); the ``accel`` magnitude limiter
    81	(E3SM-PROVENANCE constants ``tndmax``/``umcfac``, a LOOSE analog of E3SM's per-phase-speed
    82	``|c−u|/dt`` limiter — NOT
    83	E3SM-equivalent: no phase speed ``c``, one scalar magnitude, no post-limit stress reconstruction);
    84	density / ``U_mag`` floors; the scan-carry dtype pin.
    85	Non-behavioral pins: ``tests/atmosphere/hydrostatic/unit/test_hines_gwd_faithful.py``.
    86	
    87	References
    88	----------
    89	- Hines, C. O. (1997). Doppler-spread parameterization of gravity-wave
    90	  momentum deposition in the middle atmosphere. 1. Basic formulation.
    91	  J. Atmos. Solar-Terr. Phys., 59, 371-386.
    92	"""
    93	
    94	from __future__ import annotations
    95	
    96	import jax
    97	import jax.numpy as jnp
    98	
    99	from legoesm import constants
   100	from legoesm.atmosphere.physics._shared import brunt_vaisala_n_full
   101	from legoesm.atmosphere.physics.gravity_wave_drag.config import HinesConfig
   102	from legoesm.atmosphere.physics.gravity_wave_drag.output import GWDOutput
   103	
   104	# Machine-checked scheme contract (see tests/test_physics_contracts.py).
   105	__physics_contract__ = {
   106	    "summary": (
   107	        "Hines-INSPIRED non-orographic gravity-wave drag (single bulk-amplitude "
   108	        "heuristic, NOT the Doppler-spread spectrum): a launched rms wave amplitude "
   109	        "grows with 1/sqrt(rho) upward, saturates against a bulk scalar scale "
   110	        "N/m_*, and deposits the per-layer stress decrement as a drag on the flow."
   111	    ),
   112	    "inputs": {
   113	        "u": "m/s", "v": "m/s", "T": "K",
   114	        "p_full": "Pa", "p_half": "Pa", "z_full": "m", "z_half": "m",
   115	        "rho": "kg/m^3", "lat": "rad", "dt": "s",
   116	    },
   117	    "outputs": {
   118	        "du_dt": "m/s^2", "dv_dt": "m/s^2", "dT_dt": "K/s", "eps_gwd": "W/m^2",
   119	    },
   120	    "sign_convention": (
   121	        "z up. Drag opposes the wind: accel is a pure deceleration along the "
   122	        "local wind vector (du_dt*u + dv_dt*v <= 0); stress decrement "
   123	        "drag = rho*(sigma_grown^2 - sigma_new^2) is floored at 0 (a sink). "
   124	        "eps_gwd>=0 is the column KE loss returned as frictional heating "
   125	        "dT_dt = -(u*du_dt + v*dv_dt)/c_pd."
   126	    ),
   127	    # KE->heat is an EXACT local closure: the resolved mean-flow KE removed
   128	    # (-U.a) is returned exactly as frictional heating (c_pd*sum(rho*dT_dt*dz)
   129	    # == eps_gwd). But total WAVE + mean-flow ENERGY is NOT conserved: the
   130	    # launched wave is an EXTERNAL/unbudgeted source, and the Fmax cap + the
   131	    # tendency limiter discard the implied carry loss (the scan removes the
   132	    # full uncapped amplitude loss from the wave but deposits only the capped
   133	    # stress on the mean flow). Momentum is not conserved either. Hence
   134	    # "none" -- the only exact invariant is the resolved-KE->heat closure,
   135	    # pinned by the idealized test, not a total-energy conservation law.
   136	    "conserves": ["none"],
   137	    # True = AD-compatible (a defined VJP everywhere, incl. the clip/minimum
   138	    # subgradient kinks); NOT everywhere-smooth (see NUMERICS in the docstring).
   139	    "differentiable": True,
   140	    "reference": (
   141	        "Hines (1997), J. Atmos. Solar-Terr. Phys. 59, 371-386 "
   142	        "(Doppler-spread parameterization, basic formulation)"
   143	    ),
   144	    "idealized_test": (
   145	        "tests/atmosphere/hydrostatic/unit/test_gravity_wave_drag.py: rest "
   145	        "tests/atmosphere/hydrostatic/unit/test_gravity_wave_drag.py: rest "
   146	        "state -> zero tendency; du_dt*u + dv_dt*v <= 0 at every level; "
   147	        "c_pd*sum(rho*dT_dt*dz) == eps_gwd >= 0 (KE->heat closure)"
   148	    ),
   149	}

   151	
   152	def hines_gwd(
   153	    u: jax.Array,
   154	    v: jax.Array,
   155	    T: jax.Array,
   156	    p_full: jax.Array,
   157	    p_half: jax.Array,
   158	    z_full: jax.Array,
   159	    z_half: jax.Array,
   160	    rho: jax.Array,
   161	    lat: jax.Array,
   162	    dt: float,
   163	    config: HinesConfig,
   164	) -> GWDOutput:
   165	    """Compute Hines-inspired bulk GWD tendencies.
   166	
   167	    Parameters
   168	    ----------
   169	    u, v, T, p_full, p_half, z_full, z_half, rho, lat, dt, config
   170	        Standard GWD backend signature. All column arrays (ncol, nlev).
   171	
   172	    Returns
   173	    -------
   174	    GWDOutput
   175	    """
   176	    ncol, nlev = u.shape
   177	
   178	    # Brunt-Väisälä frequency at full levels
   179	    N_full = brunt_vaisala_n_full(T, p_full, z_full)
   180	
   181	    # Wind magnitude at each level
   182	    U_mag = jnp.sqrt(u ** 2 + v ** 2 + 1e-10)
   183	
   184	    # Layer thickness
   185	    dz = jnp.abs(z_half[:, :-1] - z_half[:, 1:])
   186	    dz = jnp.clip(dz, 1.0, None)
   187	
   188	    # Saturation amplitude per level:
   189	    # As the bulk wave propagates upward its amplitude grows with decreasing
   190	    # density (the code's assumed WKB invariant rho*sigma^2 = const; this is
   191	    # NOT the true momentum flux rho*<u'w'>).  Saturation occurs when the
   192	    # wave-induced velocity perturbation reaches a BULK saturation-amplitude
   193	    # scale ``sigma_sat = N / m_*`` (a velocity ~ the intrinsic phase speed;
   194	    # a heuristic, NOT Hines 1997 eq. 9's cutoff wavenumber), constant per
   195	    # column at fixed N and m_*.  An earlier formulation divided this
   196	    # by ``rho_ratio = sqrt(rho_sfc/rho) ≥ 1`` ⇒ ``sigma_sat`` *decreased*
   197	    # with altitude, the opposite of physical expectation: amplitudes
   198	    # grow with altitude (1/sqrt(rho)) so the cap should remain at least
   199	    # constant.  The /rho_ratio factor caused premature saturation aloft
   200	    # and biased the drag deposition lower in the column (audit GWD-B2).
   201	    sigma_sat = N_full / jnp.clip(config.m_star, 1e-6, None)
   202	
   203	    # Per-level WKB growth factor for the bottom-up scan.  Going from
   204	    # level (k+1) to level k (one step upward), the amplitude grows by
   205	    # ``sqrt(rho[k+1] / rho[k])`` (energy conservation rho * sigma^2).
   206	    # The carry already contains the integrated WKB amplitude from the
   207	    # surface to level k+1, so we multiply by the *inter-level* ratio,
   208	    # not the cumulative ``sqrt(rho_sfc/rho_k)``.  Multiplying by the
   209	    # cumulative factor at every step compounds the growth and
   210	    # over-amplifies the wave by a product of cumulative ratios — a
   211	    # bug masked in operational use only because the sigma_sat cap
   212	    # truncates the runaway.
   213	    rho_ratio_step = jnp.ones_like(rho)
   214	    rho_ratio_step = rho_ratio_step.at[:, :-1].set(
   215	        jnp.sqrt(jnp.clip(
   216	            rho[:, 1:] / jnp.clip(rho[:, :-1], 0.01, None), 1.0, None,  # coeff-ok: density-ratio floor
   217	        ))
   218	    )
   219	
   220	    # Bottom-up scan: propagate sigma_gw upward from surface.
   221	    # ``rho_ratio_step[:, k]`` carries amplitude from level k+1 to level k;
   222	    # at the surface (k = nlev-1) the step factor is 1 (initial condition).
   223	    def scan_fn(carry, k_rev):
   224	        sigma_gw = carry
   225	        k = nlev - 1 - k_rev
   226	
   227	        # Amplitude growth from density decrease (single-layer step)
   228	        sigma_grown = sigma_gw * rho_ratio_step[:, k]
   229	
   230	        # Smooth blend toward the saturation amplitude. ABOVE threshold
   231	        # (sigma_grown > sigma_sat) this dissipates (sigma_new < sigma_grown,
   232	        # a sink). BELOW threshold the sigmoid is small but NONZERO, so
   233	        # sigma_new = sigma_grown*(1-f)+sigma_sat*f is pulled slightly UP
   234	        # toward sigma_sat (sigma_new > sigma_grown): a weak spurious SOURCE
   235	        # in the carry. The drag floor clip(., 0, Fmax) zeroes the resulting
   236	        # negative decrement, so this sub-threshold amplitude gain is neither
   237	        # drag nor heat -- an unbudgeted carry perturbation of the smooth
   238	        # (AD) sigmoid, not a physical process (see NUMERICS in the docstring).
   239	        f_diss = jax.nn.sigmoid(
   240	            config.doppler_sharpness * (sigma_grown - sigma_sat[:, k])
   241	        )
   242	        sigma_new = sigma_grown * (1.0 - f_diss) + sigma_sat[:, k] * f_diss
   243	
   244	        # Stress decrement: ``ΔF = ρ · (σ²_grown - σ²_new)`` [Pa].  Under the
   245	        # code's ASSUMED fixed wave geometry/proportionality ``F ∝ ρσ²`` this
   246	        # reads as a stress-flux divergence between two levels of the WKB-grown
   247	        # wave; it is NOT the physical spectral flux ``F = ρ·<u'w'>`` — Hines'
   248	        # azimuthal spectrum supplies the vector covariance (the ``k/m`` sign/
   249	        # geometry) that this single-amplitude surrogate lacks.  Acceleration
   250	        # of the mean flow is then ``-ΔF / (ρ·dz)`` [m/s²].
   251	        #
   252	        # An earlier formulation used ``ρ · (σ_grown - σ_new)``, which
   253	        # has units ``kg/(m²·s)`` rather than Pa, so the downstream
   254	        # ``accel = drag / (ρ·dz)`` came out as ``1/s`` rather than
   255	        # ``m/s²`` (audit cycle 2 P1: "Hines drag dimensional
   256	        # inconsistency").  Operationally the two forms gave near-
   257	        # identical drag because Fmax saturates the upper levels in
   258	        # both, but they differ by a factor of ``σ_grown + σ_new``
   259	        # (typically 2-4×) in the sub-saturation troposphere.
   260	        #
   261	        # Clamp the lower bound to zero: the smooth ``f_diss`` sigmoid
   262	        # does not vanish exactly when ``sigma_grown < sigma_sat``, so
   263	        # without the floor a small "anti-drag" leak can appear in the
   264	        # transition region.  GWD on the mean flow is always a sink.
   265	        drag = (sigma_grown ** 2 - sigma_new ** 2) * rho[:, k]
   266	        drag = jnp.clip(drag, 0.0, config.Fmax)
   267	
   268	        # Pin the carry back to the launch-wind precision: under x64 the
   269	        # Python-float ``config.*`` constants promote ``sigma_new`` to f64, but
   270	        # the scan carry init (sigma_gw_init) is ``u.dtype`` (f32) — lax.scan
   271	        # requires carry in/out dtypes to match, so cast the carry output.
   272	        return sigma_new.astype(sigma_gw.dtype), drag
   273	
   274	    # Pin the carry dtype so the scan body stays at the input precision
   275	    # (defaulting allows x64 to silently promote the launch wind to f64).
   276	    sigma_gw_init = jnp.full((ncol,), config.total_rms_wind, dtype=u.dtype)
   277	    _, drag_stack = jax.lax.scan(scan_fn, sigma_gw_init, jnp.arange(nlev))
   278	    drag_all = drag_stack.T[:, ::-1]  # (ncol, nlev), top-first
   279	
   280	    # Convert to acceleration
   281	    accel = -drag_all / jnp.clip(rho * dz, 1e-10, None)
   282	
   283	    # Tendency limiters (E3SM gw_common.F90:642-643).  ``drag_all >= 0`` so
   284	    # ``accel`` is a pure deceleration along the wind; cap its MAGNITUDE
   285	    # without touching its sign.  The fixed ``Fmax`` momentum-flux cap divided
   286	    # by a tiny ``rho*dz`` in thin, low-density upper layers produces
   287	    # physically-implausible accelerations (hundreds of m/s/day); ``tndmax``
   288	    # is the absolute ceiling, and ``umcfac*U_mag/dt`` is a LOCAL no-reversal
   289	    # limiter (Hines is amplitude-based with no explicit phase speed ``c``, so
   290	    # this is the bulk analog of E3SM's ``umcfac*|c-u|/dt``, not the literal
   291	    # phase-speed limiter).  AD-safe (``jnp.minimum``/``jnp.abs`` subgradient
   292	    # ops; no NaN/dead grad).  NOTE: a *post-flux* limiter — where it binds the
   293	    # column drag no longer exactly equals the stress-flux divergence, but
   294	    # stays a momentum SINK (no source).
   295	    tndmax = config.tndmax_per_day / 86400.0
   296	    accel_cap = jnp.minimum(config.umcfac * U_mag / dt, tndmax)
   297	    accel = -jnp.minimum(jnp.abs(accel), accel_cap)
   298	
   299	    cos_a = u / jnp.clip(U_mag, config.U_mag_floor, None)
   300	    sin_a = v / jnp.clip(U_mag, config.U_mag_floor, None)
   301	    du_dt = accel * cos_a
   302	    dv_dt = accel * sin_a
   303	
   304	    # Frictional heating
   305	    dT_dt = -(u * du_dt + v * dv_dt) / constants.c_pd
   306	
   307	    # Column dissipation (positive-definite: KE lost by the mean flow)
   308	    eps_gwd = -jnp.sum(rho * (u * du_dt + v * dv_dt) * dz, axis=1)
   309	
   310	    return GWDOutput(du_dt=du_dt, dv_dt=dv_dt, dT_dt=dT_dt, eps_gwd=eps_gwd)

   190	    # density (the code's assumed WKB invariant rho*sigma^2 = const; this is

  2297	        """Build a JIT-compiled unified physics step with radiation sub-cycling.
  2298	
  2299	        ``rad_stop_gradient`` (radiation-as-forcing): wrap the radiation core's
  2300	        outputs (heating + TOA/surface fluxes) in ``jax.lax.stop_gradient`` so
  2301	        radiation is applied FORWARD but carries no reverse-mode gradient.
  2302	        rrtmgp's adjoint is the dominant XLA compile cost of the differentiable
  2303	        rollout (it grows with grid size — minutes at T21, >10 h at T106), yet
  2304	        the only rrtmgp-tunable param is surface albedo (2 scalars; ``tau`` is
  2305	        gray-only).  Treating radiation as a slowly-varying forcing collapses
  2306	        that compile so high-res training becomes feasible; the state loss
  2307	        still trains convection/turbulence/surface, and TOA/surface fluxes
  2308	        follow once the state matches.  Albedo, if needed, is tuned via a cheap
  2309	        separate path (forward-mode / finite-diff on the 2 scalars), NOT this
  2310	        rollout adjoint.  Default False (full adjoint, unchanged behavior).
  2311	
  2312	        SCOPE: this also makes the slab-land skin temperature ``T_land_new``
  2313	        forward-only — it is a ``compute_radiation_core`` output, so leaving it
  2314	        differentiable would drag the rrtmgp adjoint back in.  Intended (the
  2315	        radiation-driven land skin update is forcing too); moot for ocean-only
  2316	        AIMIP (``T_land`` inert).  A land run needing differentiable skin-T
  2317	        must use the full adjoint (False).
  2318	
  2319	        ``jit`` (default True) wraps the step in ``jax.jit`` — the production path.
  2320	        Pass ``jit=False`` for differentiable parameter calibration that feeds a
  2321	        TRACED value into the pipeline via an attribute the step reads (e.g.
  2322	        ``land_ml_params`` in the coupled land calibrator): a jitted step would
  2323	        capture that tracer as a closure constant and leak it across
  2324	        ``value_and_grad`` calls (``UnexpectedTracerError``).  The un-jitted step
  2325	        is inlined into the caller's ``lax.scan`` trace, so there is no separate
  2326	        compiled artefact to capture the tracer.
  2327	
  2328	        Returns a function ``step_unified(need_rad, T, p_s, q_v, q_c, q_r,
  2329	        conv_prog, u, v, sst, sic, lat, lon, day_of_year, seconds_of_day, dt,

  2333	        ``T_land`` is the slab-land skin temperature carried through the
  2334	        radiation sub-cycle; it is advanced on radiation steps and held
  2335	        constant otherwise.  Pass ``None`` (the default) for ocean-only
  2336	        runs — the land tile is then inert.  ``land_ml`` is the prognostic
  2337	        multilayer (Richards) land state pytree carried alongside the slab

  2339	        the 4th value ``land_ml_new``.  Every consumer MUST unpack all four
  2340	        returns — see ``compiled_segments`` (length-aware) and the per-step
  2341	        loop in ``model_driver``.

  2344	        ----------
  2345	        static_need_rad : bool or None, optional

    42	def _routable_keys(config_obj, candidate_keys: set) -> set:
    43	    """Candidate keys the PRODUCTION router actually routes into ``config_obj``.
    44	
    45	    Probes ``run_config_yaml._route_overrides_by_class`` (the exact function
    46	    ``apply_params_to_config`` uses) with an empty per-key override: routing
    47	    records the key in ``applied`` iff the class is PRESENT, and raises
    48	    ``SystemExit`` iff it is AMBIGUOUS (instantiated more than once) — so the
    49	    audit delegates presence/ambiguity semantics to production instead of
    50	    re-implementing the tree walk (a mirror could drift)."""
    51	    from legoesm.driver.run_config_yaml import _route_overrides_by_class
    52	
    53	    routable: set = set()
    54	    for key in candidate_keys:
    55	        applied: set = set()
    56	        try:
    57	            _route_overrides_by_class(config_obj, {key: {}}, applied=applied)
    58	        except SystemExit:
    59	            continue  # AMBIGUOUS in this tree -> production refuses to route
    60	        if key in applied:
    61	            routable.add(key)
    62	    return routable

   107	def _compute_uncovered() -> set[str]:
   108	    """Uncovered tunables, honoring run_coupled's clobber-refusal contract.
   109	
   110	    ``run_coupled._check_params_clobber`` hard-refuses routes whose overrides
   111	    ``CoupledESMDriver.setup()`` would rebuild-and-discard, so the coupled
   112	    bundle must NOT count as coverage for them:
   113	
   114	    * ``ocean.*`` — refused unconditionally (calibrate via run_omip);
   115	    * ``land.carbon.*`` — refused unconditionally (calibrate via run_lmip);
   116	    * other ``land.*`` — refused under the DEFAULT ``--land-params clm`` but
   117	      settable with ``--land-params analytical``, so the coupled route still
   118	      counts (conditional reachability, documented in the guard's error).
   119	    """
   120	    omip_keys, lmip_keys, coupled_keys = _driver_key_sets()
   121	    amap = set(build_atm_scalar_param_map())
   122	    uncovered: set[str] = set()
   123	    for m in build_registry():
   124	        if m.tunable_tier not in _TUNABLE_TIERS:
   125	            continue
   126	        key = (m.module, m.config_class)
   127	        comp = m.qualified_name.split(".")[0]
   128	        if comp == "atm":
   129	            covered = m.qualified_name in amap
   130	        elif comp == "ocean":
   131	            # run_coupled refuses ALL ocean.* (--params clobber guard), so
   132	            # only run_omip counts.
   133	            covered = key in omip_keys
   134	        elif comp == "land":
   135	            # run_coupled refuses land.carbon.* unconditionally; non-carbon
   136	            # land.* is reachable there only via --land-params analytical.
   137	            coupled_ok = (key in coupled_keys
   138	                          and not m.qualified_name.startswith("land.carbon."))
   139	            covered = key in lmip_keys or coupled_ok
   140	        else:  # ice, coupler
   141	            covered = key in coupled_keys
   142	        if not covered:
   143	            uncovered.add(m.qualified_name)
   144	    return uncovered

   201	def config_to_dict(config) -> dict:
   202	    """Generic config -> JSON-safe dict codec.
   203	
   204	    Thin delegator to the canonical home ``legoesm.driver.config.config_to_dict``
   205	    (federation carve, Step 3): a single implementation, kept here as a back-compat
   206	    entry point for callers that import it from ``forcing.amip_config``. Deferred
   207	    import avoids a forcing<->driver module-init cycle.
   208	    """
   209	    from legoesm.driver.config import config_to_dict as _impl
   210	    return _impl(config)
   211

   213	def config_from_dict(d: dict):
   214	    """Reconstruct a config from a dict written by :func:`config_to_dict`.
   215

   217	    (auto-detects ExperimentConfig vs legacy flat AMIPExperimentConfig). Deferred
   218	    import avoids a forcing<->driver module-init cycle.
   219	    """
   220	    from legoesm.driver.config import config_from_dict as _impl
   221	    return _impl(d)

   236	# ==============================================================================
   237	# Checkpoint / Restart
   238	# ==============================================================================
   239	
   240	def save_checkpoint(
   241	    path: Path,
   242	    state,
   243	    q_v: jnp.ndarray,
   244	    step: int,
   245	    day: float,
   246	    config,
   247	    diag_accumulators: dict | None = None,
   248	    q_c: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
   249	    q_r: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
   250	    carry_aux: dict | None = None,
   251	) -> None:
   252	    """Save a checkpoint for restart.
   253	
   254	    Parameters
   255	    ----------
   256	    path : Path
   257	        Output file path (.npz).
   258	    state : HydrostaticState
   259	        Atmospheric state (NamedTuple with Field members).
   260	    q_v : jax.Array
   261	        Moisture field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   262	    step : int
   263	        Current time step number.
   264	    day : float
   265	        Current simulation day.
   266	    config : ExperimentConfig or AMIPExperimentConfig
   267	        Experiment configuration (saved alongside for reproducibility).
   268	    diag_accumulators : dict, optional
   269	        Any accumulated diagnostic arrays to preserve across restart.
   270	    q_c : jax.Array, optional
   271	        Cloud water field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   272	    q_r : jax.Array, optional
   273	        Rain water field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   274	    """
   275	    # Extract state arrays
   276	    arrays = {
   277	        "T": np.asarray(state.T.data),
   278	        "u": np.asarray(state.u.data),
   279	        "v": np.asarray(state.v.data),
   280	        "p_s": np.asarray(state.p_s.data),
   281	        "phis": np.asarray(state.phis.data),
   282	        "q_v": np.asarray(q_v),
   283	        "step": np.array(step),
   284	        "day": np.array(day),
   285	    }
   286	
   287	    # Save hydrometeor fields if provided
   288	    if q_c is not None:
   289	        arrays["q_c"] = np.asarray(q_c)
   290	    if q_r is not None:
   291	        arrays["q_r"] = np.asarray(q_r)
   292	
   293	    # Save config as JSON string inside npz
   294	    arrays["config_json"] = np.array(json.dumps(config_to_dict(config)))
   295	
   296	    # Save diagnostic accumulators if provided
   297	    if diag_accumulators:
   298	        for k, v in diag_accumulators.items():
   299	            arrays[f"diag_{k}"] = np.asarray(v)
   300	
   301	    # Save carry auxiliary fields (held radiation, target_moisture, etc.)
   302	    if carry_aux:
   303	        for k, v in carry_aux.items():
   304	            arrays[f"carry_{k}"] = np.asarray(v)
   305	
   306	    np.savez(str(path), **arrays)

   309	def load_checkpoint(
   310	    path: Path,
   311	    grid,
   312	    sigma,
   313	) -> tuple:
   314	    """Load a checkpoint and reconstruct state.
   315	
   316	    Parameters
   317	    ----------
   318	    path : Path
   319	        Checkpoint file path (.npz).
   320	    grid : CubedSphereGrid
   321	        Grid (must match checkpoint resolution).
   322	    sigma : SigmaCoordinate
   323	        Vertical coordinate (must match checkpoint nlev).
   324	
   325	    Returns
   326	    -------
   327	    state : HydrostaticState
   328	    q_v : jax.Array
   329	    step : int
   330	    day : float
   331	    config : AMIPExperimentConfig
   332	    diag_accumulators : dict
   333	    q_c : jax.Array or None
   334	    q_r : jax.Array or None
   335	    """
   336	    from legoesm.core.field import Field
   337	    from legoesm.core.state import HydrostaticState
   338	
   339	    from legoesm.core.precision import get_policy
   340	    _storage_dtype = get_policy().storage
   340	    _storage_dtype = get_policy().storage
   341	
   342	    data = np.load(str(path), allow_pickle=True)
   343	
   344	    T = jnp.array(data["T"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   345	    u = jnp.array(data["u"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   346	    v = jnp.array(data["v"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   347	    p_s = jnp.array(data["p_s"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   348	    phis = jnp.array(data["phis"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   349	    q_v = jnp.array(data["q_v"], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   350	
   351	    step = int(data["step"])
   352	    day = float(data["day"])
   353	
   354	    dims_3d = ("face", "x", "y", "level")
   355	    dims_2d = ("face", "x", "y")
   356	
   357	    state = HydrostaticState(
   358	        u=Field(data=u, name="u", dims=dims_3d, units="m/s"),
   359	        v=Field(data=v, name="v", dims=dims_3d, units="m/s"),
   360	        T=Field(data=T, name="T", dims=dims_3d, units="K"),
   361	        p_s=Field(data=p_s, name="p_s", dims=dims_2d, units="Pa"),
   362	        phis=Field(data=phis, name="phis", dims=dims_2d, units="m^2/s^2"),
   363	    )
   364	
   365	    # Restore config
   366	    config_str = str(data["config_json"])
   367	    config = config_from_dict(json.loads(config_str))
   368	
   369	    # Restore diagnostic accumulators
   370	    diag_accumulators = {}
   371	    for key in data.files:
   372	        if key.startswith("diag_"):
   373	            diag_accumulators[key[5:]] = data[key]
   374	
   375	    # Restore hydrometeor fields if present
   376	    q_c = jnp.array(data["q_c"], dtype=_storage_dtype) if "q_c" in data.files else None
   377	    q_r = jnp.array(data["q_r"], dtype=_storage_dtype) if "q_r" in data.files else None
   378	
   379	    # Restore carry auxiliary fields (held radiation, etc.).  The
   380	    # stateful-physics carries (issue #413) keep their STORED dtype:
   381	    # the prognostic-spectral GWD spectrum is persisted at the default
   382	    # float dtype (its kernel's internal scan breaks on a storage-
   383	    # downcast carry), and a storage cast here would also make the
   384	    # restart non-bit-exact for the physics memory.  Everything else
   385	    # (held radiation, conv_prog, T_land, …) keeps the legacy storage
   386	    # cast.
   387	    _keep_stored_dtype = ("tke", "qke", "gwd_spectrum")
   388	    carry_aux = {}
   389	    for key in data.files:
   390	        if key.startswith("carry_"):
   391	            _name = key[6:]
   392	            if _name == "conv_prog_scheme":
   393	                # Scheme tag for the convection carry (issue #413) —
   394	                # a plain string, not a float array.
   395	                carry_aux[_name] = str(data[key])
   396	            elif _name in _keep_stored_dtype:
   397	                carry_aux[_name] = jnp.array(data[key])
   398	            else:
   399	                carry_aux[_name] = jnp.array(data[key], dtype=_storage_dtype)
   400	
   401	    return state, q_v, step, day, config, diag_accumulators, q_c, q_r, carry_aux

CLAUDE.md-144-- Cross-backend: dtype, x64, unsupported kernels, comm semantics.

CLAUDE.md-146-## Hygiene/Imports/Tests (audit)
CLAUDE.md-147-- Every new `.py` ≥1 direct unit test importing+exercising leaf module (tendencies for physics schemes — not just integration via factory). No `__init__.py` re-export / `supported_matrix.py` / factory dispatch add without same-PR test. Block PRs growing untested-LIVE count.
CLAUDE.md-148-- New config dispatch (Literal + factory in `integration.py`): test via public config.
CLAUDE.md:149:- **New user-tunable config field → same-PR CLI flag in every affected run script.** Rule applies to `ExperimentConfig`/`DycoreConfig`/`OutputConfig` fields in `run_amip.py`, `OceanExperimentConfig`/`KPPConfig`/`VerticalMixingConfig` in `run_omip.py`, and `MultiLayerLandConfig` sub-configs in `run_lmip.py`. "User-tunable" = any float/int/str/bool field a user would reasonably change for a sensitivity run (excludes: internal-only flags such as `debug_precision`/`diagnostics_perf_mode`, unimplemented stubs like `carbon_cycle` in AMIP, and parallel-milestone-gated fields like `distributed_mode=spmd`). Each new flag also needs: (1) wiring in `build_config_from_args` / the equivalent config-builder, (2) a round-trip test in the corresponding `tests/unit/test_run_*_cli.py`, and (3) a `validate_strict` membership check if it is a scheme Literal. FLOAT tunables with a `__param_spec__` need no flag: all four MIP drivers take `--config` (dests, choices-validated) + `--params` (registry-qualified `scheme_key.field`, bounds-validated; atm via the flattened-scalar map). Reachability is machine-audited by `tests/unit/test_params_reachability_audit.py` against the shrink-only `_params_reachability_baseline.py` (a new spec'd tunable unreachable in its component's drivers goes red) — the #691 "CLI flag gaps" debt closure.
CLAUDE.md-150-- Removing module: also remove `__init__.py` re-export, `supported_matrix.py` entry, dispatch, test file, `__pycache__`.
CLAUDE.md-151-- No deprecated backward-compat wrappers — update call sites. No thin dispatch-only wrappers (`X_utils.py` re-exporting `X.py`) — inline/factor. Real branching across callers (`land/stomata_utils.py`) legit. Grid variants legit when genuinely different numerics; indexing-only copy-paste forbidden.
CLAUDE.md-152-- **No top-level cross-package imports from `core/` to `runtime/`/`parallel/`/`driver/`/`training/`/`experiments/`.** Why: `from legoesm.runtime.backend import ...` at top of `core/precision.py` triggered `runtime/__init__.py` → `runtime.precision` → `core.precision` mid-init, breaking isolated pytest. Use function-scope deferred imports.
CLAUDE.md-153-- **No import of private (`_`-prefixed) symbols across modules.** Promote (drop underscore + `__init__.py` re-export) or factor public wrapper. Mutable singletons (`grids.halo._halo_backend`/`_mpi_topology`, `cubesphere_exchange._spmd_mesh`): use accessors (`get_halo_backend`/`get_mpi_topology`/`get_spmd_mesh`), never import the global. Audit: `grep -rE "from legoesm\.[^ ]+ import [^,]*\b_[a-z]" src/legoesm/ packages/ | grep -v " as _"` = 0 (line-grep misses multi-line/function-scope/`_UPPER` imports); CI ratchet `tests/test_no_private_cross_imports.py` (AST, incl. function-scope; dunder-exempt; shrink-only allowlist EMPTY since 2026-06-10 — keep it empty).
CLAUDE.md-154-- **Test-only modules MUST be acknowledged.** Not wired into factory/`__init__.py`/prod driver: (a) wire same PR, (b) move to `_future/` + docstring + xfail/skip, or (c) delete.
--

     1	# legoESM Claude Memory
     2	
     3	## Role
     4	Senior JAX+ESM dev. Skeptical, verify-first. Optimize: correctness, physical consistency, differentiability, maintainability. Prefer `opusplan`/`opus` high effort for dycore/physics/parallel/debug. Fast mode off.
     5	
     6	## Repo Facts
     7	- Differentiable ESM in JAX: atm, ocean, land, sea ice, coupler, DA, ML.
     8	- End-to-end `jax.grad` compat = goal. Never break autodiff/JIT/pytree.
     9	- Mass conservation hard. Energy/momentum when scheme permits.
    10	- Parallel entry: `ParallelRuntime.create()`.
    11	- Grids: cubed-sphere, lat-lon, Gaussian/spectral, Voronoi/MPAS, icosahedral.
    12	
    13	## Training (`src/legoesm/training/`)
    14	- 3 modes: physics param tune, neural GCM, SFNO+dycore.

    53	## JAX
    54	- Pure pytree fns. `lax.scan` time integration. `vmap`/batched arrays over Python loops on array dims. `jnp.where`/`lax.cond`/`fori_loop`/`scan` not Python control flow on traced.
    55	- **Feature gating exception** (`fix_mass`, `fix_moisture`): Python `if` on static bool in closure — NOT `jnp.where` (traces both branches). `jnp.where` only for data-dependent traced selection.

    58	- **Buffer donation + `jax.grad`**: `donate_argnums` conflicts reverse-mode AD. JIT fn inside `jax.grad`/`eqx.filter_value_and_grad` → provide non-donating variant (`.raw`). See `build_segment_fn`.
    59	- **Closures vs explicit args**: closure captures = compile-time consts. Per-iter changing val (SST, solar) → pass as traced arg. See `SegmentForcing`.

    61	## Earth System
    62	- Conservation, metric consistency, staggered-grid consistency, halo correctness = first-class.
    63	- No silent clip/damp/coerce unless justified+validated.
    64	- Preserve units, sign conventions, monotonicity/positivity, hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic.
    65	- Cubed-sphere/curvilinear: assume edge+metric errors first.
    66	- Physics coupling: column closure + consistent flux signs.
    67	- DA/diff: preserve smoothness. No gratuitous nondiff.
    68	- **Sign-convention check MANDATORY on every equation/flux/tendency edit.** Before declaring done on any code touching a PDE term, flux, source/sink, BC, or budget update: (1) state the coordinate convention in scope (z up/down, flux positive-up/down/into-body) as a comment at the term; (2) walk EACH term and confirm its sign matches that convention — gravity vs capillary/diffusion divergence, top vs bottom BC, source vs sink, the `±` in `state = state ± dt·tend`; (3) confirm the budget closes (`in − out − Δstorage = 0`) and exchanged fluxes carry the SAME sign at both ends of a coupling (land runoff `+into ocean` must arrive `+into ocean`). A comment label and the code must agree — a flux commented "upward" computed as downward is a defect, fix the label or the math. Mechanical gate where feasible: a sign/conservation unit test (analytic column, manufactured solution, or `assert` budget residual ≈ 0) — passing norms alone never certify a sign is right (a flipped flux can still be small). Common flips: z-axis direction, evap positive-up vs moistening, brine/salt vs freshwater dilution, stress atmospheric vs ocean convention (`-tau`), free-drainage vs gravity double-count.

    95	## Validation
    96	- Narrowest test after edits. Numerical changes: analytical/benchmark > unit tests alone. `JAX_ENABLE_X64=1` unless float32/Metal task.
    97	- Dycore: Williamson, Galewsky, Jablonowski-Williamson, DCMIP, Held-Suarez, ocean benchmarks.
    98	- Conservation/reductions/coupler: mass+energy diagnostics.
    99	- Parallel: unsharded vs sharded, single-rank vs MPI.
   100	- Too expensive: say what ran/didn't, residual risk.
   101	- **CRITICAL — Controlled comparison: change ONE variable, hold the eval protocol FIXED to the baseline.** To claim a change (resolution, params, scheme, days) improved/degraded/"is comparable" vs a prior result, keep EVERYTHING else byte-identical to that baseline: forcing data + its sampling (years/days/hours/climatology), evaluation grid, metric definition (bias vs RMSE), region masks, timestepping. A metric that moved because the protocol/sampling changed is a **CONFOUND, not a result** — NEVER compare a number computed on one sampling/grid/metric to a number from another and call the difference an effect. If a resource limit (network cap, compute, time) forces a lighter or different sampling, **re-run the BASELINE at that SAME sampling before comparing** — a fresh baseline is cheap insurance; a confounded claim is not. Before writing "improved"/"degraded"/"better"/"comparable" vs any earlier number, explicitly confirm the two configs differ ONLY in the variable under test; if you cannot, say so and claim NO direction. Report the full config (data+sampling, grid, days/steps, params, metric) next to every number so the reader knows exactly what is being compared. Assuming two runs are comparable when the setup drifted is the error that turns "we improved it" into "we degraded it."
   102	- **CRITICAL — Precision gate for comparison/skill/causal claims (do NOT be sloppy — 2026-07-20 EC-site lesson).** (a) **Harness self-check FIRST**: before reporting a NEW scheme's skill vs a validated baseline, run the KNOWN baseline through your OWN harness and confirm it reproduces the baseline's established/published number (±small tol). If your harness scores a validated scheme wildly off — e.g. two-leaf H looked "broken" (NSE≈−1) when the paper figure tracks obs — the HARNESS is wrong; fix it BEFORE any new-scheme claim. (b) **Match the reference metric EXACTLY**: metric aggregation (daily-mean vs half-hourly point-wise NSE), window (multi-year JJA vs one summer), masks (valid-forcing) are ALL part of the protocol. Report the SAME metric the reference used, plus any alternative, WITH the sample N. A single-window point-wise metric is NOT a skill verdict, and never rank schemes by a metric that punishes one scheme's known artifact (point-wise scatter/spikes) while ignoring the dimension of interest (mean diurnal shape). (c) **Never let a QC mask flatter one side**: if you drop a scheme's unphysical spikes from scoring, report BOTH the failures-penalized primary score AND the separately-labeled plausible-only sensitivity score. (d) **Do NOT INFER causal origin — INSTRUMENT it**: "the spikes come from X" requires LOGGING X and the alternatives (raw vs intermediate vs final), not deduction from reading one code path; "correctly hooked up" requires reading the FULL path, not the entry point. (e) **Label every claim CONFIRMED (evidence shown) vs PLAUSIBLE (inferred)** — adversarial review WILL refute over-confident inferences; state uncertainty up front rather than presenting a verdict table that a five-minute check overturns.
   103	- **CRITICAL — Visual verify spatial/grid artifacts**: passing tests+norms NECESSARY ≠ SUFFICIENT for cubed-sphere ops, halo exchange, diffusion coeffs, grid metrics. Edge artifacts/cube imprint/grid-scale noise only detected visually (v-wind W2, wind_speed W5). Run `--only sw --grid cubed_sphere --quick` + inspect PNGs vs baseline. Norms can improve while artifacts worsen. Never claim "tests pass, edge fixed" from pytest alone.
   104	- **Diffusion sensitivity**: div damping + hyperdiff AMPLIFY halo errors at cubed-sphere face boundaries. Check W2 v-wind visually when touching `_hyperdiff_cube`, `_div_damp_cube`, diffusion params.
   105	- **Visual-regression gate (cube imprint)**: `scripts/validate/visual_regression.py --check` numericises the W2 v-wind cube-imprint check (SSIM + per-panel perceptual hash + edge-artifact ratio vs tiny committed ref in `tests/visual_baselines/`). Deterministic metric math gated in CI (`tests/test_visual_regression_metrics.py`); full cube-SW `--check` runs as a NIGHTLY non-blocking CI job until tolerances are calibrated across CI hardware. Tiny numeric baselines (.npy+json) ARE tracked — the one carve-out to "no tracked visual baselines".

   107	## Domain Architect vs Syntax Engine (AI guardrails)
   108	See `docs/architecture/ai_guardrails/domain_architect_vs_syntax_engine.md`. Doctrine: the human dictates the *logic* (units, signs, conserved qty, valid scheme sets, references, acceptance criteria); AI fills the *body*; every declared invariant is checked **mechanically** so violations fail LOUDLY. Each gate is a **tripwire, not a proof** and ships a synthetic-violation self-test (provably non-vacuous). NON-NEGOTIABLE harness (extend, never weaken; budgets/TODOs shrink only):
   109	- **Spec-first physics contracts**: every physics scheme module declares `__physics_contract__` (units/signs/conserves/differentiable/reference/idealized_test); `tests/test_physics_contracts.py` partitions all `*/physics/*.py` into EXCLUDED / CONTRACT_TODO(shrink-only) / annotated — a NEW physics file must ship a contract or be classified. Author the contract + acceptance test BEFORE the body.
   110	- **Atmospheric parameterization edits are high-risk**: run codex adversarial review, #477 truth-tier tendency validators, conservation tests, and the equilibrium-SCM-RCE realism harness before merge. A NEW scheme must pass the RCE realism gate or enter its shrink-only TODO partition with a reason.
   111	- **CI ratchets** (AST + self-test, via shared `tests/_ratchet_audit.py`): `test_no_hardcoded_constants` (constants only from `legoesm.constants`), `test_no_saturation_reimpl` (saturation only from `thermo`), `test_dispatch_hardening` (no scheme guard silently deleted), `test_validate_strict_coverage` (no scheme field skips fail-early validation). Escape: real `# const-ok:`/`# satcurve-ok:` comment.
   112	- **Local hooks** (`.claude/hooks/`, wired in `settings.json`): PreToolUse blocks an edit adding a banned constant/saturation prefactor to a `.py` (fail-open); Stop reminds (once/session) to run the mandatory codex review on uncommitted numerics/physics. CI remains authoritative (a `Bash` heredoc bypasses the hook, not CI).
   113	- **Best coding practices = use the existing system**, not a parallel one: ruff/mypy, import-linter (`alerting="error"`), inline-import budgets, pre-impl grep + shared utilities (no re-derivation), every new `.py` gets a unit test, slopbuster sweeps, iterate-with-codex on substantial changes.

   128	## File Layout (audit — enforce on EVERY new file; no random files)
   129	- **New scripts go in the correct `scripts/` bucket — NEVER `scripts/` root or repo root.** Buckets: `run/` (prod drivers), `matrix/` (test-matrix registries), `bench/` (perf/profiling/scaling), `plot/` (plot/replot/regen), `validate/` (non-matrix validators/verifiers/conservation checks), `data/` (download/build/prepare forcing+IC), `experiment/` (init/reproduce/templates/machine-detect/fetch), `cluster/` (SLURM `.sbatch` job wrappers, e.g. `cluster/omip_nemo/`). Pick the bucket by what the script DOES. New bucket needs a real category, not a dumping ground. See `scripts/README.md`.
   130	- **Debug / throwaway / one-off → `scripts/tmp/` ONLY** (eventually deleted): `_*`-prefixed probes, `diag_*`/`diagnose_*`, per-iteration scratch. Never at `scripts/` root. `_probe_*.py` is gitignored.
   131	- **No new files dumped at repo root.** Root keeps ONLY: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `FEDERATION.md`, `project_status.md` (generated), `pyproject.toml`/lockfile/dotfiles. Everything else has a home.
   132	- **No `.md` notes accumulating at repo root → `docs/`.** Dev-notes, change logs, faithfulness/audit trackers (`*_faithful.md`, `*_checks.md`, review logs) live under `docs/`. Reference by BASENAME so code comments survive the move.
   133	- **No runtime outputs in git.** `diagnostics/`, `logs/`, `**/logs/`, `results/`, `checkpoints/`, `output/`, `*.zarr`/`*.nc`, root `*.png`/`*.pdf`/`*.svg` gitignored. Visual-regression baselines stay in LOCAL working copies, regenerated on demand — not tracked. Never `git add -f` a runtime artifact.
   134	- **Source stays under `packages/<pkg>/legoesm/`** (federation namespace). New subpackage → update `tests/test_federation_plan.py` same PR.
   135	- **Do NOT "flatten" `packages/<pkg>/legoesm/<subpkg>/` → `packages/<pkg>/` — the double name is LOAD-BEARING, not redundant.** Editable installs (the dev/test workflow) require on-disk path == import path, and hatchling REFUSES a prefix-*adding* `sources` remap in dev mode (`ValueError: Dev mode installations are unsupported when any path rewrite in the sources option changes a prefix rather than removes it`; editables#20). So `packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/` is the only layout where `import legoesm.atmosphere` resolves under `pip install -e`. Flattening to keep `legoesm.*` builds a wheel but breaks editable dev; flattening to bare `import atmosphere` means rewriting ~23k import sites + dropping the namespace. Verified 2026-07-13 — don't re-attempt. `src/legoesm/` is the SANCTIONED root meta-package (the `legoesm.*` TOP-LEVEL modules: `constants`, `config`, `cli`, `registry`, `dycore_factory`, …), same load-bearing reason — NOT a stray `src/` to remove. "Never add source at `src/`" means don't create NEW `src/` trees for component code; the existing `src/legoesm/` root stays.

   140	- Instability: CFL, boundary, metric, halo, pressure-gradient, diffusion, dtype.
   141	- Conservation drift: flux form, weights, reductions, state updates before fixers.
   142	- Differentiability: control flow, shape changes, side effects, checkpointing, nondiff branches.
   143	- Perf regression: retrace, host callbacks, scatters, sharding, Python loops.
   144	- Cross-backend: dtype, x64, unsupported kernels, comm semantics.

   146	## Hygiene/Imports/Tests (audit)
   147	- Every new `.py` ≥1 direct unit test importing+exercising leaf module (tendencies for physics schemes — not just integration via factory). No `__init__.py` re-export / `supported_matrix.py` / factory dispatch add without same-PR test. Block PRs growing untested-LIVE count.
   148	- New config dispatch (Literal + factory in `integration.py`): test via public config.
   149	- **New user-tunable config field → same-PR CLI flag in every affected run script.** Rule applies to `ExperimentConfig`/`DycoreConfig`/`OutputConfig` fields in `run_amip.py`, `OceanExperimentConfig`/`KPPConfig`/`VerticalMixingConfig` in `run_omip.py`, and `MultiLayerLandConfig` sub-configs in `run_lmip.py`. "User-tunable" = any float/int/str/bool field a user would reasonably change for a sensitivity run (excludes: internal-only flags such as `debug_precision`/`diagnostics_perf_mode`, unimplemented stubs like `carbon_cycle` in AMIP, and parallel-milestone-gated fields like `distributed_mode=spmd`). Each new flag also needs: (1) wiring in `build_config_from_args` / the equivalent config-builder, (2) a round-trip test in the corresponding `tests/unit/test_run_*_cli.py`, and (3) a `validate_strict` membership check if it is a scheme Literal. FLOAT tunables with a `__param_spec__` need no flag: all four MIP drivers take `--config` (dests, choices-validated) + `--params` (registry-qualified `scheme_key.field`, bounds-validated; atm via the flattened-scalar map). Reachability is machine-audited by `tests/unit/test_params_reachability_audit.py` against the shrink-only `_params_reachability_baseline.py` (a new spec'd tunable unreachable in its component's drivers goes red) — the #691 "CLI flag gaps" debt closure.
   150	- Removing module: also remove `__init__.py` re-export, `supported_matrix.py` entry, dispatch, test file, `__pycache__`.
   151	- No deprecated backward-compat wrappers — update call sites. No thin dispatch-only wrappers (`X_utils.py` re-exporting `X.py`) — inline/factor. Real branching across callers (`land/stomata_utils.py`) legit. Grid variants legit when genuinely different numerics; indexing-only copy-paste forbidden.

   154	- **Test-only modules MUST be acknowledged.** Not wired into factory/`__init__.py`/prod driver: (a) wire same PR, (b) move to `_future/` + docstring + xfail/skip, or (c) delete.

RESOLVED 2026-05-29 (direct tests added): `coupler/surface_energy.py`, `ocean/dynamics/barotropic_common.py`, `atmosphere/dynamics/sfno_pe.py`, `atmosphere/dynamics/tracer_transport_mpas.py`; `atmosphere/physics/convection/_triggers.py` + `timestepping/tridiagonal.py` already covered.
   158	
   159	## Constants/Params (audit)
   160	- **All physical constants in `src/legoesm/constants.py`.** New constant (T, ρ, c, L, k, μ, EOS coeff, Schmidt#, R_earth) MUST be added BEFORE use. No constants in `config.py`/fn bodies/test fixtures/plotters/notebooks even with `# = constants.X` comment.
   161	- **`getattr(..., "X", <literal>)` fallbacks count as hardcoded.** Use `getattr(grid, "radius", constants.R_earth)`. Same `setattr`/`dict.get`/`kwargs.get`.
   162	- **No hardcoded physical constants in fn sigs/bodies in `src/legoesm/`.** No `def f(g=9.80616, ...)` → `g: float = constants.g` or config NamedTuple. NamedTuple defaults SHOULD reference constants. Tunable scheme params (sigmoid sharpness, τ, drag) stay in config NamedTuple.
   163	- **No hardcoded tunable params in physics bodies.** Sigmoid sharpness, τ, Louis coeffs, KPP epsilon, emissivity, drag → scheme `*Config` NamedTuple. Exempt: safety floors (`eps=1e-30`), math constants (`0.5`, `2.0`), category lookup tables (PFT `L_v` in `surface_params.py`) with doc.
   164	- **No `273.15` for C↔K in prod.** Use `constants.T_freeze`. `T_freeze_ocean=271.35 K` in `ocean/eos.py` = only intentional exception.
   165	- **Tests+scripts+plotters same rule.** `from legoesm import constants`. No `9.80616`, `7.292e-5`, `6.371e6` literals.
   166	- **Sigmoid sharpness/transition widths in JAX hot loops forbidden as magic numbers.** Inside `scan_step`/`cond`: fn kwarg with doc default OR scheme `*Config` field. Ex: `compute_moist_adiabat(lcl_sigmoid_width_pa=100.0)`, `PlumeConfig.active_sigmoid_sharpness=1e4`, DM95 `transition_width_frac=0.1` on `dm95_taper`/`dm95_taper_scalar`/`_triad_taper`.
   167	- **Saturation re-impl in forcing modules forbidden.** Use `legoesm.thermo.saturation_mixing_ratio`/`saturation_vapor_pressure`.
   168	
   169	### Parameter hygiene — declare per category at file top + machine-readable tunable/fixed split (gated)
   170	Two CI tripwires enforce this (extend, never weaken; baselines shrink-only): `tests/test_no_inline_physics_coeffs.py` (+`_inline_coeff_baseline.py`) and `tests/test_param_specs.py` (+`_param_spec_baseline.py`).
   171	- **No inline empirical coefficient in a physics function body OR signature default.** Across `*/physics/*`, `land/`, `ice/`, `coupler/`: every float literal (and int `|v|>16`) inside a function scope is flagged. Move it to (a) a scheme `*Config` NamedTuple field if tunable/scheme-defining, (b) a module-level `_UPPER_SNAKE` constant/table block (published fits/tables: Sutherland, Hall-Pruppacher, Morel-Berthon, Jerlov, KK2000) with a provenance comment if a fixed published constant, or (c) a real `# coeff-ok: <reason>` (reason REQUIRED) for a genuine numerics one-off. Exempt: math {0,0.25,0.5,1,2,3,4,6}, exact conversions, `|v|<=1e-6` floors, `|v|>=1e20` guards, subscript indices, Pow exponents, small ints (indices/counts).
   172	- **Per-file layout (consistent placement):** docstring → imports → `__physics_contract__` → `__param_spec__` → fixed `_UPPER_SNAKE` constant/table blocks (under `# --- <category> (<reference>) ---` comments) → `*Config` NamedTuple(s) with fields grouped by the same category comments (snake_case + unit suffixes) → functions whose bodies read ONLY `cfg.<field>` / `constants.*` / exempt math. Kwarg-default literals → reference a module constant or config field (a Name in the signature, not a literal).
   173	- **Every physics scheme `*Config` declares `__param_spec__`** (module-level pure dict literal next to the NamedTuple). Per float field: `units`, `bounds (lo,hi)`, `tunable_tier`, `transform` (sigmoid/softplus/none), `category`, `reference`, `shape` (None or dim key like `n_pft` for variable-size array params), optional `legacy_name`. A NEW config module must ship a spec or be classified in `PARAM_SPEC_TODO` (shrink-only). Inclusion is computed: only `:float`-annotated fields are spec-eligible.
   174	- **Tunable/fixed split (the continuum), classify the SAME way every time:**
   175	  - `tunable_tier 1` (**core**) = params already trained in practice / well-posed (surface albedos, ice strength `P_star`, gray optical depths, bulk exchange `C_H`/`C_E`).
   176	  - `tunable_tier 2` (**extended**) = clear closure knobs with literature bounds (relaxation timescales τ, entrainment/drag/autoconv rate coefficients, thresholds, emissivity, roughness).
   177	  - `tunable_tier 0` / `excluded` (with a reason string) = NOT trainable: numerics floors/caps/regularisers, smoothing widths, measurement conventions (e.g. MOST 10 m), and anything **iteration-coupled** (mEVP `alpha`/`beta`, EVP `T_evp` couple to the subcycle count).
   178	  - The collector selects tiers `1..N` (`build_trainable_params(config, tier="core"/"extended"/"aggressive", include=, exclude=)`); flip a param's status with a 1-line `tunable_tier` edit. See [[param-hygiene-spec-effort]].
   179	- **Loop-iteration COUNTS are never config/trainable** → module constant (e.g. `_N_EVP_DEFAULT = 120`), not a config field, not a kwarg-default literal. Structurally guaranteed: ints are not spec-eligible, so an iteration count can never reach the trainable collector. See [[loop-counts-never-trainable]].
   180	- **A tunable closure whose default is a `constants.X` reference** (e.g. `S_ice_new = constants.S_ice_bulk_default`) is *eligible* (may be a `__param_spec__` param with explicit bounds + tier) though not *required* (the AST gate won't force it). Expose genuine calibratable closures; keep environmental references (ocean salinity) fixed/excluded.
   181	- **Trained values inject via the config pytree, not new signatures:** `params.to_overrides()` → `param_collector.apply_param_overrides(physics_config, overrides)` (`NamedTuple._replace`) INSIDE the loss so leaves are TRACED (SegmentForcing doctrine); production keeps static Python-float leaves (constant-folded, no retrace). Register a newly-specced module in `param_collector.SPEC_MODULES` (drift-tested).
   182	
   183	## Naming
   184	- Surface T = `T_sfc` everywhere. No new `T_surface`/`Ts`.
   185	- Driver/config schema field names match runtime field. New tunable: same name in `driver/config.py`, scheme config NamedTuple, YAML schema (consistent `hyperdiff_coeff`).
   186	- **Same name + different units = bug magnet (audit).** Unit hint (`_C`, `_K`, `_s`, `_days`, `_m`, `_km`): use everywhere. New C-vs-K args MUST carry `_C`/`_K`. Config fields sharing base (`tau_*`, `T_*`, `c_*`, `C_*`) MUST have consistent unit suffixes OR distinct names.
   187	- **snake_case all NamedTuple fields**, even capitalized symbols (CAPE, CIN, MSE, TKE). `SBMConfig.CAPE_threshold` → `cape_threshold`.
   188	- **Renaming a tunable `__param_spec__` field = rename the field AND its spec key together + add `legacy_name: <old>`.** The spec key must equal the float field name (`test_param_specs`), so a half-rename goes red; `legacy_name` documents the prior name for any externally-saved tuned JSON. (2026-06-22: `CarbonConfig.T_opt→T_opt_C`/`T_width→T_width_C`, `StomataConfig.T_opt_jarvis→T_opt_jarvis_C`/`T_range_jarvis→T_range_jarvis_C` — Celsius fields gaining the `_C` suffix.)
   189	- **`tau_`/`τ` prefix is valid for wind/wave STRESS [Pa], not timescales only.** Ocean wind stress and GWD launch stress (`tau_0`, `tau_max`) are standard GFD τ notation — do NOT auto-rename them to `stress_*`. The real anti-pattern is MIXED units under one `tau_*` family inside a single config without unit suffixes; fix by suffixing the timescale members (`_s`), not the stresses.

A bare `else: <default>` here silently runs different physics on a typo. Lock each new guard in `tests/test_dispatch_hardening.py::BASELINE_DISPATCHERS` (grow-only) so it can't be silently deleted.

   204	## Common Mistakes
   205	**NamedTuple fields**: verify actual field. `PhysicsOutput.precip` not `precipitation`. `hasattr` guard silently degrades. Adding field to `SegmentCarry`: update every call site. `grep -rn "SegmentCarry(" --include="*.py"`.

   209	- Preferred: `land_mask_override` to `rest_state_latlon_cgrid_ocean()` at construction.
   210	- Post-construction: `replace_land_mask(state, new_mask)` from `init_latlon_cgrid.py` — atomic update 3 masks.

   214	- Never build closures in training loops. `build_segment_fn` creates new fn per call → inside `for epoch`/`_loss_fn` recompiles each iter. Build once outside; pass changing vals as args.
   215	- Helper fns inside `lax.scan` body: Python defs in `_single_step` recreated each trace. Move to module scope.

Adding field cross-cutting: NamedTuple def, `pack_carry`, `unpack_carry` docstring, per-step Python ref loop in `test_compiled_segments.py`, `test_scale_tpu_compat.py`, `test_scale_jit_health.py`, direct `SegmentCarry(...)` in validation tests. New diagnostic fields (`max_cfl`) reset to zero at segment start, not accumulated.

  1244	    # Horizontal q_v smoothing on the MPAS lane [m^2/s]; 0 = off (byte-
  1245	    # identical; appended at the tuple END to preserve the positional ABI).
  1246	    # The MPAS lane historically had NO horizontal moisture smoothing (the FV
  1247	    # lanes smooth q_v every step in their step factories) — the confirmed
  1248	    # missing third suspect behind the cell-scale CWV recharge/discharge
  1249	    # speckle (2026-07-23).  Applied post-step as an UNWEIGHTED SCVT del2 (∇²)
  1250	    # + a q>=0 floor: monotone / positivity-preserving under the setup-time
  1251	    # CFL guard (the floor is then a no-op, to roundoff), and it conserves the per-level
  1252	    # mixing-ratio area integral sum_c A_c q_c (exact in exact arithmetic; to
  1253	    # floating-point roundoff — ~1e-7 relative in fp32).  It is NOT column-
  1254	    # water-vapour (CWV = sum_c A_c dp_c q_c/g) conserving: across a surface-
  1255	    # pressure gradient an unweighted del2 redistributes a little water mass
  1256	    # (bias set by the humidity–terrain correlation), so this is an explicitly
  1257	    # NON-conservative grid-scale filter — monitor the water budget if used in
  1258	    # long runs.  Unweighted (not dp-weighted) is REQUIRED: the default hybrid
  1259	    # coordinate's surface-layer dp goes <= 0 for p_s below ~2/3 p_ref over
  1260	    # high terrain, which a dp-weighted form would divide by (Inf/NaN).  It is
  1261	    # a del2 (∇²), not the FV lanes' scale-selective del4 (∇⁴): del2 is
  1262	    # monotone under the explicit guard (hence the exact per-level integral)

    91	    """Return trainable parameter constraints reachable under the given schemes.

    93	    Filters out parameters that the selected physics configuration can

   101	    - an active turbulence scheme owns the surface fluxes, so the bulk
   102	      ``C_H``/``C_E`` only train with ``turbulence_scheme="none"``;
   103	    - only SBM has scheme-specific convection parameters.
   104	
   105	    Parameters
   106	    ----------
   107	    convection_scheme : str
   108	        Convection scheme name: "sbm", "dca", "kuo", "mass_flux", "edmf",
   109	        "none".
   110	    radiation_scheme : str
   111	        Radiation scheme name: "gray", "rrtmgp" (alias "rrtmg"), "none".
   112	    turbulence_scheme : str
   113	        Turbulence scheme name ("none" enables the bulk surface pair).
   114	
   115	    Returns
   116	    -------
   117	    list[ParamConstraint]
   118	    """
   119	    radiation = "rrtmgp" if radiation_scheme == "rrtmg" else radiation_scheme
   120	
   121	    constraints: list[ParamConstraint] = []
   122	    if radiation == "gray":
   123	        constraints += _GRAY_RADIATION_TRAINABLE
   124	    if radiation in ("gray", "rrtmgp"):
   125	        constraints += _ALBEDO_TRAINABLE
   126	    if turbulence_scheme == "none":
   127	        constraints += _BULK_SURFACE_TRAINABLE
   128	    if convection_scheme == "sbm":
   129	        constraints += _SBM_TRAINABLE
   130	    return constraints

   133	def sigmoid_to_range(raw: jax.Array, lo, hi) -> jax.Array:
   134	    """Map unconstrained raw value(s) to [lo, hi] via sigmoid.
   135	
   136	    ``lo``/``hi`` may be scalars (broadcast over an array ``raw``) or tuples /
   137	    arrays of per-element bounds; conversion through ``jnp.asarray`` keeps the
   138	    transform elementwise and differentiable for array parameters."""
   139	    lo = jnp.asarray(lo, dtype=raw.dtype)
   140	    hi = jnp.asarray(hi, dtype=raw.dtype)
   141	    return lo + (hi - lo) * jax.nn.sigmoid(raw)
   142	
   143	
   144	def range_to_sigmoid(val: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
   145	    """Inverse (scalar): map a [lo, hi] value to unconstrained raw (logit)."""
   146	    t = (val - lo) / (hi - lo)
   147	    t = max(min(t, 0.999), 0.001)  # clamp for numerical stability
   148	    import math
   149	    return math.log(t / (1.0 - t))
   150	
   151	
   152	def range_to_sigmoid_array(val: jax.Array, lo, hi) -> jax.Array:
   153	    """Inverse (array-safe): map [lo, hi] value(s) to unconstrained raw (logit),
   154	    elementwise, with the same 0.001/0.999 clamp as the scalar form. Used by the
   155	    spec collector to seed array-valued raw parameters."""
   156	    val = jnp.asarray(val)
   157	    lo = jnp.asarray(lo, dtype=val.dtype)
   158	    hi = jnp.asarray(hi, dtype=val.dtype)
   159	    t = jnp.clip((val - lo) / (hi - lo), 0.001, 0.999)
   160	    return jnp.log(t / (1.0 - t))
   161

   163	class TrainablePhysicsParams(eqx.Module):
   164	    """Learnable physics parameters as an Equinox module.
   165	
   166	    Stores unconstrained raw values; apply_constraints() returns
   167	    physical values in valid ranges.
   168	
   169	    Usage::
   170	
   171	        params = TrainablePhysicsParams.from_defaults()
   172	        physical = params.as_dict()  # {name: constrained_value}
   173	        segment_kwargs = params.to_segment_kwargs()  # ready for build_segment_fn
   174	    """
   175	    raw_values: dict[str, jax.Array]
   176	    constraints: list[ParamConstraint] = eqx.field(static=True)
   177	
   178	    @staticmethod
   179	    def from_defaults(
   180	        constraints: list[ParamConstraint] | None = None,
   181	    ) -> TrainablePhysicsParams:
   182	        """Create from default values in the tuning registry."""
   183	        if constraints is None:
   184	            constraints = DEFAULT_TRAINABLE
   185	
   186	        # Resolve dtype from precision policy (default float32).
   187	        try:
   188	            from legoesm.core.precision import get_policy
   189	            param_dtype = get_policy().compute
   190	        except Exception:
   191	            param_dtype = jnp.float32
   192	
   193	        raw = {}
   194	        for c in constraints:
   195	            # Look up default from registry, fallback to midpoint
   196	            if c.name in TUNING_PARAMETERS:
   197	                default = TUNING_PARAMETERS[c.name].default
   198	            else:
   199	                default = (c.min_val + c.max_val) / 2.0
   200	
   201	            if c.transform == "sigmoid":
   202	                raw[c.name] = jnp.array(
   203	                    range_to_sigmoid(default, c.min_val, c.max_val),
   204	                    dtype=param_dtype,
   205	                )
   206	            elif c.transform == "softplus":
   207	                # Overflow-safe inverse softplus: log(exp(y)-1) = y + log1p(-exp(-y)).
   208	                # The naive ``float(log(exp(default)-1))`` overflows to inf for
   209	                # default >~ 700 (even in fp64) — large timescales / lengths /
   210	                # concentrations — seeding the trained leaf with inf. Mirrors
   211	                # ``param_collector._seed_raw``.
   212	                y = max(float(default), 1e-6)
   213	                raw[c.name] = jnp.array(
   214	                    y + float(jnp.log1p(-jnp.exp(-y))),
   215	                    dtype=param_dtype,
   216	                )
   217	            else:
   218	                raw[c.name] = jnp.array(default, dtype=param_dtype)
   219	
   220	        return TrainablePhysicsParams(raw_values=raw, constraints=constraints)

   273	    if model_type == "hydrostatic":
   274	        return _make_hydrostatic_gwd(gwd_config, dt)
   275	    elif model_type == "nonhydrostatic":
   276	        return _make_nonhydrostatic_gwd(gwd_config, dt)
   277	    elif model_type == "spectral_pe":
   278	        return _make_spectral_pe_gwd(gwd_config, dt)
   279	    elif model_type == "mpas":
   280	        return _make_mpas_gwd(gwd_config, dt)
   281	    else:
   282	        raise ValueError(
   283	            f"Unknown model_type: {model_type!r}. "

   299	               -> HydrostaticTendencies
   300	
   301	    When *phys_state* is passed, the GWD wave action spectrum is read
   302	    from ``phys_state.gwd_spectrum`` and the updated spectrum is
   303	    returned as the second element of the result tuple.
   304	    """
   305	    scheme_name, gwd_fn, scheme_config = get_gwd_fn(gwd_config)
   306	    is_prognostic = scheme_name == "prognostic_spectral"
   307	    is_ml = scheme_name == "ml_emulator"
   308	    # ``e3sm_cam`` shares the orographic launch signature (accepts the
   309	    # optional per-column ``h_topo_col`` subgrid orographic stddev keyword);
   310	    # its config selects the orographic vs frontal/convective source internally.
   311	    #
   312	    # NOTE: the ``e3sm_cam`` frontal source needs a per-column frontogenesis
   313	    # function ``frontgf_col`` and the convective (Beres) source needs a
   314	    # convective heating profile ``netdt_col`` (and, for bit-faithfulness, the
   315	    # offline ``mfcc`` table).  This GWD factory's ``(state, grid, sigma)``
   316	    # signature does not currently carry those fields, so from here only the
   317	    # orographic source is driven; the frontal/convective sources are exercised
   318	    # through the public ``e3sm_cam_gwd(..., frontgf_col=, netdt_col=,
   319	    # mfcc_table=)`` entry point (wiring the convective-heating coupling through
   320	    # the physics pipeline is a separate integration task and must not reach

   324	    # sums their tendencies; ``combined_spectrum`` marks the sub-case that also
   325	    # threads the prognostic wave-action spectrum.

   327	    combined_spectrum = is_combined and gwd_carries_spectrum(scheme_name)

   250	        """Initialize all knobs at (or just inside) their canonical defaults.
   251	
   252	        Edge-of-range knobs whose canonical default sits within
   253	        ``sigmoid_margin`` (5% of the range) of a bound are interiorized to
   254	        that margin, so the initial inverse-sigmoid gradient is non-trivial and
   255	        the optimizer can actually move them (a default exactly at a bound maps
   256	        to a saturated logit with ~0 gradient).  Example: ``gray_sfc_emissivity``
   257	        canonical 1.0 initializes at 0.975.  Mid-range knobs initialize exactly
   258	        at their canonical default.  This trades a small physical perturbation
   259	        at the edges for trainability — see the ``sigmoid_margin`` note below.
   260	
   261	        Parameters
   262	        ----------
   263	        spatial_surface : bool
   264	            If True, initialize a :class:`AIMIPSpatialSurfaceParams`
   265	            bundle for the surface and surface-radiation knobs.
   266	        spatial_init_std : float
   267	            Standard deviation of the Gaussian initialization in
   268	            spatial-coefficient space.  ``0.0`` keeps the spatial
   269	            field equal to the scalar baseline at step zero (useful
   270	            for sanity-checking that ``spatial_surface=True`` reduces
   271	            to the scalar mode at init); a small positive value
   272	            (e.g. 0.02) breaks the zero-gradient symmetry and lets
   273	            the optimizer explore the spatial degrees of freedom
   274	            immediately.  Only used when ``spatial_surface=True``.
   275	        spatial_seed : int
   276	            PRNG seed for the spatial-coefficient initialization.
   277	            Only used when ``spatial_surface=True`` and
   278	            ``spatial_init_std > 0``.
   279	        """
   280	        scheme_defaults = _canonical_scheme_defaults()
   281	        try:
   282	            from legoesm.core.precision import get_policy
   283	
   284	            param_dtype = get_policy().compute
   285	        except Exception:
   286	            param_dtype = jnp.float32
   287	
   288	        # v7: clamp the inverse-sigmoid input away from the bounds so
   289	        # the initial gradient is non-trivial even when the canonical
   290	        # default sits at the saturation edge.  Without this,
   291	        # ``sfc_emissivity`` (canonical default 0.98 or 1.0) maps to
   292	        # raw values where ``sigmoid'`` is ~1e-2 or less and the
   293	        # bias-penalty loss cannot move the knob.  5% of the range
   294	        # is a small physical perturbation (emissivity 0.98 -> 0.975
   295	        # in [0.5, 1.0]) but bumps the sigmoid gradient by ~3x.
   296	        sigmoid_margin = 0.05
   297	        raw: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
   298	        for c in AIMIP_CLASSICAL_CONSTRAINTS:
   299	            default = scheme_defaults.get(c.name, 0.5 * (c.min_val + c.max_val))
   300	            margin = sigmoid_margin * (c.max_val - c.min_val)
   301	            default_clamped = min(
   302	                c.max_val - margin, max(c.min_val + margin, default),
   303	            )
   304	            raw[c.name] = jnp.asarray(
   305	                range_to_sigmoid(default_clamped, c.min_val, c.max_val),
   306	                dtype=param_dtype,
   307	            )
   308	        spatial = None
   309	        if spatial_surface:
   310	            spatial = AIMIPSpatialSurfaceParams.from_defaults(
   311	                dtype=param_dtype,
   312	                init_std=spatial_init_std,
   313	                key=jax.random.PRNGKey(int(spatial_seed)),
   314	            )
   315	        return AIMIPClassicalParams(
   316	            raw_values=raw,
   317	            constraints=AIMIP_CLASSICAL_CONSTRAINTS,
   318	            spatial_surface=spatial,
   319	        )

   663	        per-rank backends, so this rides the same mechanism). No-op for
   664	        warm-rain runs. Returns a NEW dict (does not mutate ``self._carry_aux``).
   665	        Only valid for FULL-LOCAL state (serial / replicated / per-rank
   666	        distributed); band-gathered lat-lon-MPI checkpoints must guard instead,
   667	        since these tracers are rank-local bands (mirrors the T_land limitation).
   668	        """

   683	        # soil/snow/carbon columns ride carry_aux (namespaced land_ml_*) so a

   685	        # cold-starting. No-op for slab-land runs (_land_ml_state is None).

   744	        # leak forward into the next _checkpoint_carry_aux() re-save.
   745	        popped = {k[len("land_ml_"):]: self._carry_aux.pop(k) for k in keys}

 succeeded in 511ms:
     1	"""Spec-first guard: every physics scheme ``*Config`` declares a ``__param_spec__``.
     2	
     3	The user's request that motivates this gate: the tunable-vs-fixed status of every
     4	physics parameter must be *machine-readable* (so a training loop can select which
     5	to optimize) and easy to flip. We record that next to each scheme ``*Config``
     6	NamedTuple as a module-level ``__param_spec__`` dict literal — the parameter-level
     7	twin of ``__physics_contract__`` (this file mirrors ``test_physics_contracts.py``).
     8	
     9	The spec carries NO default *values* — the NamedTuple field default is the single
    10	numeric source of truth. The spec adds only what the NamedTuple cannot express:
    11	units, optimisation bounds, a tunability tier (the continuum: 0=fixed, 1=core,
    12	2=extended, 3=aggressive), the constraint transform, a category, a literature
    13	reference, an optional array ``shape`` dimension key, and an optional flat
    14	``legacy_name`` alias. Example::
    15	
    16	    __param_spec__ = {
    17	        "SBMConfig": {
    18	            "scheme_key": "sbm",          # globally unique
    19	            "excluded": {"smooth_trigger_sharpness": "numerics: gate width"},
    20	            "params": {
    21	                "tau_c": {
    22	                    "units": "s", "bounds": (1800.0, 21600.0),
    23	                    "tunable_tier": 1, "transform": "sigmoid",
    24	                    "category": "closure", "reference": "Frierson (2007)",
    25	                    "shape": None, "legacy_name": "sbm_tau_c",
    26	                },
    27	            },
    28	        },
    29	    }
    30	
    31	**Inclusion is computed, not enumerated.** A class is *spec-required* iff it
    32	subclasses ``NamedTuple`` and has at least one ``: float``-annotated field whose
    33	default folds to a number (a ``constants.X`` / nested-config / int / str / bool
    34	default is auto-exempt — it cannot be a stray tunable). **Only float fields are
    35	spec-eligible**, which is the structural guarantee that loop-iteration counts and
    36	other discrete integers (``N_evp``, ``bulk_n_iter``, ``n_categories``, ...) can
    37	NEVER be exposed to a tuning / backprop loop: they are non-differentiable control
    38	flow, an ``int`` field cannot appear in a spec's ``params`` (it is not in the
    39	float-default set, so it is flagged as an orphan), and the trainable collector
    40	only ever materialises float params. A module with at least one
    41	spec-required class must EITHER carry a ``__param_spec__`` covering every such
    42	class's every float field (in ``params`` or ``excluded``) OR appear in the
    43	SHRINK-ONLY ``PARAM_SPEC_TODO``. A NEW config module is in neither, so it FAILS
    44	until it ships a spec — the forcing function. ``PARAM_SPEC_TODO`` burns to empty.
    45	
    46	Validation is AST-only (no imports, no side effects): defaults are read from the
    47	NamedTuple's AST so ``bounds ⊇ default`` is checked without importing the module.
    48	Self-tests prove non-vacuity.
    49	"""
    50	
    51	from __future__ import annotations
    52	
    53	import ast
    54	import collections
    55	
    56	import pytest
    57	
    58	from tests import _ratchet_audit as ra
    59	from tests._param_spec_baseline import PARAM_SPEC_FIELD_BASELINE
    60

   101	def _is_namedtuple(cls: ast.ClassDef) -> bool:
   102	    for b in cls.bases:
   103	        if isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "NamedTuple":
   104	            return True
   105	        if isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "NamedTuple":
   106	            return True
   107	    return False
