   110	def _float_default_fields(cls: ast.ClassDef) -> dict[str, float]:
   111	    """``{field_name: folded_default}`` for every ``: float``-annotated field
   112	    whose default folds to a number. A ``constants.X`` / nested-config / name
   113	    default folds to ``None`` and is auto-exempt — so is any non-float annotation."""
   114	    out: dict[str, float] = {}
   115	    for n in cls.body:
   116	        if not (isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name)):
   117	            continue
   118	        if not (isinstance(n.annotation, ast.Name) and n.annotation.id == "float"):
   119	            continue
   120	        if n.value is None:
   200	            # reference (not AST-resolvable); the structural lo<hi check still
   201	            # runs, and the collector clamps the resolved value at seed time.
   202	            errs.append(f"default {default} outside sigmoid bounds {bounds}")
   203	    elif isinstance(bounds, tuple) and len(bounds) == 2 and all(
   204	        isinstance(b, tuple) for b in bounds
   205	    ):
   206	        # per-element bounds: (lo_tuple, hi_tuple) of equal length
   207	        lo_t, hi_t = bounds
   208	        if len(lo_t) != len(hi_t):
   209	            errs.append(f"per-element bounds length mismatch: {bounds}")
   210	    elif tier >= 1:
   211	        errs.append(f"tier>=1 requires (lo, hi) bounds, got {bounds!r}")
   212	    return errs

   215	def validate_param_spec(
   216	    spec,
   217	    required: dict[str, dict[str, float]],
   218	    eligible: dict[str, set[str]] | None = None,
   219	) -> list[str]:
   220	    """Schema + completeness errors for one module's ``__param_spec__``.
   221	
   222	    ``required`` = ``{Class: {field: literal_default}}`` — float fields with a
   223	    *folding* (literal) default that MUST be classified. ``eligible`` =
   224	    ``{Class: {all float field names}}`` — any ``: float`` field (incl. those
   225	    whose default is a ``constants.X`` reference), which MAY appear in
   226	    ``params``/``excluded`` without being an orphan. This lets a genuinely
   227	    tunable closure that happens to default to a constant (e.g.
   228	    ``S_ice_new = constants.S_ice_bulk_default``) be exposed as a spec param,
   229	    while still not FORCING constants-default fields into the spec. When
   230	    ``eligible`` is omitted it falls back to ``required`` (the strict set)."""
   231	    if spec == "__UNPARSEABLE__":
   232	        return ["__param_spec__ is not a pure literal (AST literal-eval failed)"]

   234	        return ["__param_spec__ must be a dict keyed by Config class name"]
   235	    eligible = eligible or {}

   237	    # Orphan classes: a spec entry for a class with no spec-eligible float fields.
   238	    for cls_name in spec:

   240	            errors.append(f"spec names class {cls_name!r} with no float fields")
   241	    # Validate every class that is required OR eligible (the latter covers a class
   242	    # whose float fields all default to ``constants.X`` — it is not FORCED into the
   243	    # spec, but if it appears it must still be fully schema-validated, not skipped).
   244	    for cls_name in sorted(set(required) | set(eligible)):
   245	        fields = required.get(cls_name, {})
   246	        cls_eligible = eligible.get(cls_name, set(fields))
   247	        if cls_name not in spec:
   248	            if cls_name in required:
   249	                errors.append(f"class {cls_name!r} is spec-required but absent from spec")
   250	            continue  # an eligible-only class is optional in the spec
   251	        entry = spec[cls_name]
   252	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   253	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: entry must be a dict")
   254	            continue
   255	        keys = set(entry)
   256	        missing = _REQUIRED_CLASS_KEYS - keys
   257	        extra = keys - _REQUIRED_CLASS_KEYS - _OPTIONAL_CLASS_KEYS
   258	        if missing:
   259	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: missing keys {sorted(missing)}")
   260	        if extra:

   262	        sk = entry.get("scheme_key")
   263	        if not isinstance(sk, str) or not sk.strip():
   264	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: scheme_key must be a non-empty string")
   265	        params = entry.get("params", {})
   266	        excluded = entry.get("excluded", {})
   267	        if not isinstance(params, dict):
   268	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: params must be a dict")
   269	            params = {}
   270	        if not isinstance(excluded, dict):
   271	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: excluded must be a dict")
   272	            excluded = {}
   273	        # Completeness: every float field classified exactly once.
   274	        classified = set(params) | set(excluded)
   275	        unclassified = sorted(set(fields) - classified)
   276	        if unclassified:
   277	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: float fields not in params/excluded: {unclassified}")
   278	        both = sorted(set(params) & set(excluded))
   279	        if both:
   280	            errors.append(f"{cls_name}: fields in both params and excluded: {both}")
   281	        orphan = sorted(classified - cls_eligible)

   284	        for ename, reason in excluded.items():
   285	            if not isinstance(reason, str) or not reason.strip():

   110	def _float_default_fields(cls: ast.ClassDef) -> dict[str, float]:
   111	    """``{field_name: folded_default}`` for every ``: float``-annotated field
   112	    whose default folds to a number. A ``constants.X`` / nested-config / name
   113	    default folds to ``None`` and is auto-exempt — so is any non-float annotation."""
   114	    out: dict[str, float] = {}
   115	    for n in cls.body:
   116	        if not (isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name)):
   117	            continue
   118	        if not (isinstance(n.annotation, ast.Name) and n.annotation.id == "float"):
   119	            continue
   120	        if n.value is None:
   121	            continue
   122	        folded = ra.fold_numeric(n.value)
   123	        if folded is not None:
   124	            out[n.target.id] = folded
   125	    return out

   128	def spec_required_classes(src: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
   129	    """``{ClassName: {float_field: default}}`` for module-level NamedTuple
   130	    subclasses that have at least one float-default (literal) field — the fields
   131	    a spec MUST classify."""
   132	    tree = ast.parse(src)
   133	    out: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
   134	    for node in tree.body:
   135	        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and _is_namedtuple(node):
   136	            fields = _float_default_fields(node)
   137	            if fields:
   138	                out[node.name] = fields
   139	    return out

   142	def all_float_field_names(src: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
   143	    """``{ClassName: {every ``: float`` field with a default}}`` — the spec-
   144	    ELIGIBLE set (superset of ``spec_required_classes``): also includes fields
   145	    whose default is a ``constants.X`` reference (not AST-foldable). A genuinely
   146	    tunable closure that defaults to a constant (``S_ice_new =
   147	    constants.S_ice_bulk_default``) may be listed in a spec's ``params`` without
   148	    being flagged as an orphan, but is not FORCED into the spec."""
   149	    tree = ast.parse(src)
   150	    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   151	    for node in tree.body:
   152	        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and _is_namedtuple(node):
   153	            names = {
   154	                n.target.id
   155	                for n in node.body
   156	                if isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign)
   157	                and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name)
   158	                and isinstance(n.annotation, ast.Name)
   159	                and n.annotation.id == "float"
   160	                and n.value is not None
   161	            }
   162	            if names:
   163	                out[node.name] = names
   164	    return out

I’ve completed the cross-lane trace. The material blockers are the missing calibration-map/audit work, the custom spectral-override seed mismatch, unvalidated newly-live values, the dead `N_ref` catalog entry, and a positional ABI break from inserting fields mid-`NamedTuple`.
codex
1. **CONFIRMED-BUG — calibration `--params` path remains silently inert for all newly live GWD knobs.**  
   `gwd_config_for` now threads the values into kernels, but `_ATM_SCALAR_PARAM_MAP` has no GWD entries: `packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/run_config_yaml.py:177-239`. Its rationale explicitly says `_resolve_gwd` patches only a few fields (`:169-171`), which is now stale. Consequently calibration YAML cannot reach:
   - `atm.gwd.HinesConfig.total_rms_wind`
   - `atm.gwd.HinesConfig.Fmax`
   - `atm.gwd.McFarlaneConfig.directional_spread`
   - `atm.gwd.McFarlaneConfig.tau_max`

   The first three are explicitly listed as uncovered in `tests/unit/_params_reachability_baseline.py:184-186,258`; adding mappings requires removing those baseline entries under the shrink-only audit (`tests/unit/test_params_reachability_audit.py:120-160`). `tau_max` is tier 3 (`.../gravity_wave_drag/config.py:170`), so the loader accepts a map entry but the tier-1/2 audit will not enforce it.

   Smallest fix: add the four map entries, remove the three tier-1/2 baseline entries, and extend `test_atm_scalar_map_is_pipeline_threaded` (`tests/unit/test_params_config_loader.py:140-225`) with GWD scheme selectors/readback. Its current selector/readback tables only support cloud/convection/microphysics, so adding GWD map entries alone will fail.

2. **CONFIRMED-BUG — the generic physics-state seed ignores a nested GWD override.**  
   MPAS and spectral now use the resolver, but the generic/stateful seed still creates a bare config at `packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:9418`. `init_physics_state` sizes and initializes `gwd_spectrum` from `prognostic_spectral.n_azimuths`, `n_wavenumbers`, and `launch_flux` (`packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/physics_state.py:296-311`).

   A valid `gravity_wave_drag_override` may customize those nested values (`packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:1235-1242,2053-2072`). The resolved pipeline expects its override dimensions and raises on an inconsistent seed (`packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/physics_pipeline.py:1602-1624`); restore has a related shape guard at `model_driver.py:9433-9445`. A changed `launch_flux` with unchanged dimensions is worse: it silently seeds the wrong flux.

   Smallest fix: replace the bare construction at `model_driver.py:9418` with `gwd_config_for(cfg)`. Add a regression using an override with non-default azimuths, wavenumbers, and launch flux.

3. **CONFIRMED-BUG — newly live scalar inputs have no finite/range validation.**  
   The new Hines fields are accepted directly from CLI as arbitrary floats (`scripts/run/run_amip.py:1259-1273`) and none of the five overlay values are checked by `ExperimentConfig.validate_strict` (`packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:1278-2245`). They now enter Hines at `hines.py:265-276` and McFarlane launch/saturation calculations at `mcfarlane.py:224,387-391,414-420`.

   The existing parameter metadata already defines bounds for `total_rms_wind`, `Fmax`, `directional_spread`, and `tau_max` (`.../gravity_wave_drag/config.py:118-133,151-174`). `k_wave` has none.

   Smallest fix: add finite/range checks in `validate_strict`, using the existing parameter bounds and a defined positive finite policy for `k_wave`; test negative, zero where invalid, infinity, and NaN. Your claimed sign flip needs one correction: negative `Fmax` is physically invalid, but Hines’ final limiter forces drag-direction acceleration via `-minimum(abs(accel), accel_cap)` (`hines.py:295-305`), so it does not simply reverse momentum forcing.

4. **CONFIRMED-BUG — `mcfarlane_k_wave` remains outside the parameter-spec and calibration contract.**  
   `McFarlaneConfig.k_wave` is live (`.../gravity_wave_drag/config.py:399-415`) but absent from both `params` and `excluded` (`:151-174`). Its computed `math.pi` default bypasses the AST-based required-field test (`tests/test_param_specs.py:31-44,215-280`). Therefore it has no canonical bounds, no qualified `--params` name, and no reachability-audit coverage, despite now being threaded by the resolver.

   Smallest fix: add a `__param_spec__` entry with an agreed range/tier, then map it through `_ATM_SCALAR_PARAM_MAP` and add reachability tests. Resolve the existing range disagreement first: old tuning uses `1e-5..2e-4` (`packages/ml/legoesm/tuning.py:491-504`), while AIMIP uses `1e-5..5e-4` (`packages/ml/legoesm/training/aimip_params.py:113`).

5. **CONFIRMED-BUG, pre-existing — `mcfarlane_N_ref` is a fully dead advertised tuning knob.**  
   It exists on `ExperimentConfig` (`packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:990`) and is registered as a physical tuning parameter with a misleading closure description (`packages/ml/legoesm/tuning.py:505-515`).
